--- title: "Week 3: From Base R to `sf`" subtitle: "GIS for Spatial Data Science" author: - name: "Christy Hsu" email: th1010@georgetown.edu date: 2026-09-09 week: 3 categories: - "Workshop Sessions" execute: echo: true freeze: true sidebar: mainnav format: html: output-file: "w3-idx.html" css: styles.css toc: true df-print: kable revealjs: output-file: "w3-slides.html" css: styles.css slide-number: true scrollable: true df-print: kable code: echo: true eval: true --- ## Intro to Coding Workshop! ## Outline for Today - Base R syntax and coding style - R data types and data structures - Working with **Vectors** and **Data Frames** ## Base R syntax and coding style ## `print()` and comment out ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} "Welcome to R Coding Workshop!" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Welcome to R Coding Workshop!" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} print("Welcome to R Coding Workshop!") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Welcome to R Coding Workshop!" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} 2025 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2025 ``` ::: ::: - `⌘` + `/`: Commenting ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 2025 # command + forward slash to comment out ``` ::: ## Variables `<-`: initialize a variable and assign a value ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # variable_name <- variable_value x <- 1984 y <- "World Geodetic System" ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} - R variable naming ::: ## R Data Types `class()` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - **"numeric"** - double - integer - **"character"** - **"logical"** ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} print(class(x)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "numeric" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} print(class(y)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} z <- class(x) == class(y) print(class(z)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "logical" ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} - Operators and Logical Operators - Type Casting ::: ## R Data Structures - Vector - Matrix - Array - Factor - List - Data Frame ## Starting with *Vectors* :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Ways to create a vector - `c()` - `seq(from, to, by)` - `:` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} v1 <- c( "Bryce Canyon", "Canyonlands", "Arches", "Zion", "Capitol Reef" ) v2 <- 1:5 v2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 2 3 4 5 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} v3 <- seq(21.9, 25.3, 0.1) is.vector(v2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Subsetting a Vector - Indexing ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # v1 <- c( # "Bryce Canyon", "Canyonlands", "Arches", "Zion", "Capitol Reef" # ) v1[1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Bryce Canyon" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} v1[-1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Canyonlands" "Arches" "Zion" "Capitol Reef" ``` ::: ::: - Subsetting using Logical Vectors ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} v4 <- 1:12 bool_v4 <- v4 > 8 v4[bool_v4] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 9 10 11 12 ``` ::: ::: - Access by name ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} names(v4) <- month.abb v4["Jan"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Jan 1 ``` ::: ::: ## Data Frame objects - Thinking of `data.frame` as a collection of column vectors Ways to create a df ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mth_df <- data.frame( mth = 1:12, mth_str = month.abb ) mth_df ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| mth|mth_str | |---:|:-------| | 1|Jan | | 2|Feb | | 3|Mar | | 4|Apr | | 5|May | | 6|Jun | | 7|Jul | | 8|Aug | | 9|Sep | | 10|Oct | | 11|Nov | | 12|Dec |
::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mth_df |> class() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "data.frame" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} - import external tabular dataset ::: ## `data.frame` attributes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} utah_df <- data.frame( national_park = v1, lat = c( 37.640621053549125, 38.478777627059635, 38.6167568289248, 37.200271934321734, 38.291603924096385 ), lon = c( -112.16957627116382, -109.8251716515892, -109.61982474559946, -112.98700616100083, -111.2619347149233 ) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} head(utah_df, 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|national_park | lat| lon| |:-------------|--------:|---------:| |Bryce Canyon | 37.64062| -112.1696| |Canyonlands | 38.47878| -109.8252|
::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # nrow() and ncol() dim(utah_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} colnames(utah_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "national_park" "lat" "lon" ``` ::: ::: ## Subsetting `data.frame` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} print(utah_df[, 1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Bryce Canyon" "Canyonlands" "Arches" "Zion" "Capitol Reef" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} print(utah_df[1, ]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` national_park lat lon 1 Bryce Canyon 37.64062 -112.1696 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} print(utah_df$national_park) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Bryce Canyon" "Canyonlands" "Arches" "Zion" "Capitol Reef" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} utah_df[["national_park"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Bryce Canyon" "Canyonlands" "Arches" "Zion" "Capitol Reef" ``` ::: ::: ## R List - A vector that allows to have elements of different data type - Nested ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(utah_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` national_park lat lon Length:5 Min. :37.20 Min. :-113.0 Class :character 1st Qu.:37.64 1st Qu.:-112.2 Mode :character Median :38.29 Median :-111.3 Mean :38.05 Mean :-111.2 3rd Qu.:38.48 3rd Qu.:-109.8 Max. :38.62 Max. :-109.6 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(utah_df[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "data.frame" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" collapse="true"} ![](sf-wkt.png) ::: ## Getting to `sf` and a map ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(sf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Linking to GEOS 3.13.0, GDAL 3.8.5, PROJ 9.5.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(mapview) utah_sf <- st_as_sf( utah_df, coords = c('lon', 'lat'), crs = 4326 ) utah_sf |> mapview() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} utah_sf ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|national_park |geometry | |:-------------|:--------------------------| |Bryce Canyon |POINT (-112.1696 37.64062) | |Canyonlands |POINT (-109.8252 38.47878) | |Arches |POINT (-109.6198 38.61676) | |Zion |POINT (-112.987 37.20027) | |Capitol Reef |POINT (-111.2619 38.2916) |
::: ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" collapse="true"} - prelude to `factor` class: How were the points colored? Why are we having a legend on the map? - How to avoid presenting this map ![](bad-vis.png) :::
